title: Clay Peak
summary: Challenge your skills as you ride your motorcycle or OHV on a variety of terrains in this OHV play area. Numerous trails, hill climbs and race courses will help you hone your abilities. Several competitive events are held throughout the year. This BLM area is managed by Payette County under a Recreation and Public Purposes lease.

title: Hells Canyon Wilderness

It is primarily managed by the U.S. Forest Service with approximately 940 acres managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM). title: Mann Creek Reservoir
summary: Mann Creek Reservoir is formed by Mann Creek Dam , which is part of the Mann Creek Project. title: Nez Perce National Historic Trail
summary: Congress established the Nez Perce National Historic Trail Historic Trail in 1986. It stretches from Wallowa Lake, Oregon, across Idaho to the Bear Paw National Historic Trail in Chinook, Montana. Before and after Lewis and Clark, the Nez Perce homeland extended throughout central Idaho, northeast Oregon and southeast Washington. title: Oxbow/Brownlee
summary: Oxbow and Brownlee Reservoirs provide boating, fishing, and camping opportunities along the Snake River. Oxbow Reservoir (13 miles long) is accessed from Cambridge, Idaho. Brownlee Reservoir (57 miles long) and be accessed from either Cambridge, on the north, or from Weiser, Idaho from the south. There is limited access in this general area.

title: Payette River Corridor
summary: Flowing from the central Idaho mountains, the Payette River and its various forks offers a variety of river related recreational opportunities. The BLM and Forest Service jointly manage the Main Payette and South Fork Payette Rivers to provide public river access primarily for white-water boating. title: Powder Wild and Scenic River
summary: Flowing 11.7 miles from Thief Valley dam to highway 203 in Oregon’s Baker County, the wild and scenic Power River cuts a weathered canyon in paces up to 500 feet deep.
